Food boxes and the shop

We hand out food boxes every Saturday. The boxes have rice, beans, fruit and bread. We pack them on Friday night with help from our friends at the school. Each box feeds a family of four for about a week.

You do not need to sign up. Just come to the hall on Elm Street between ten and two. Bring a bag if you can. If you cannot carry the box, tell us and we will help you to your car or the bus stop.

We also run a small shop where you can pick what you need. The shop is open on Tuesday and Thursday. It has milk, eggs, soap and other things that do not fit in a box. Everything in the shop is free.

Kids can come to our homework club after school. It runs from three to five on weekdays. Our helpers are teachers and students from the town. They help with reading, math and science, and there is a snack for everyone.

If you want to help, we need people on Friday nights and Saturday mornings. You can come once or every week. We will show you what to do when you get here. Most people find it fun, and you will make new friends.

On the last Friday of each month we cook a big meal for everyone. You can eat with us in the hall or take a plate home. We cook soup, rice and a stew, and there is always cake. Kids eat first, then everyone else.

Some of our food comes from farms near the town. The farmers bring us what they cannot sell, like apples with spots or carrots that are too big. It is all good to eat, and it would go to waste if we did not take it.

We are open in the snow and in the heat. If the weather is very bad we will post a note on the door and on our page. Call us if you are not sure, and we will tell you if we are open that day.
